meta.title: Mill: better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied

marble bust of Socrates ancient sculpture

beats.text: If happiness is the goal of life, here's a trap: a pig, well fed, seems perfectly happy.
So is the good life just maximum pleasure? Mill, a utilitarian, said no — not all pleasure is equal.
There are lower pleasures — food, comfort, ease — and higher ones: thought, art, love, meaning.
How do we know the higher ones are better? Ask anyone who has truly tasted both. They never trade down.
The higher pleasures cost more. They can leave you restless, searching, dissatisfied.
"Better to be Socrates dissatisfied," Mill wrote, "than a fool satisfied."
A gnawing hunger for something greater may be worth more than an easy, comfortable contentment.
